facts.value: To convey communicative and intercultural foreign language skills, refresh and complete existing basic knowledge of the English language, and provide subject vocabulary as well as an initial insight into general aspects of the economy in English-speaking countries.

The FOUNDATION level consists of the course WE1A. All Foundation courses have the same level of difficulty (target level B1.2 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages) and are content-wise the same. They are suitable for students who have no or very little knowledge of Business English.
Completion of level A2/B1 of the GER or 26 – 40 points in the placement test.
It is recommended to take the placement test before registration to ensure proper course placement.
The reading and writing component of the course will be assessed in a 90-minute written exam in the last week of the semester. A graded certificate is issued for passing the exam.

In the Business English Foundation course, participants learn vocabulary and expressions specifically for the business world. A variety of exercises aim to promote linguistic and conceptual understanding of current topics and lay the foundation for discussions and written exercises on various economic subjects.
Unit 1 – What is Microeconomics?; Unit 2 – Economic Indicators; Unit 3 – Business Cycle; Unit 4 – Retail Banking; Unit 5 – Retail.
90 Euro for WE1A Foundation (13 double hours, including final exam).
This course will not be offered in the winter semester 2026/27.

The KEYSTONE level consists of the parallel courses WE2A – WE2D. All Keystone courses have the same level of difficulty (target level B2.1 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages) and are content-wise the same. They are suitable for students who already possess knowledge of Business English.
Completion of level B1 of the GER or 41 – 60 points in the placement test.
The reading and writing component of the course will be assessed in a 90-minute written exam in the last week of the semester. A graded certificate is issued for passing the exam.

In the Business English Keystone course, participants learn vocabulary and expressions specifically for the business world. A variety of exercises aim to promote linguistic and conceptual understanding of current topics and lay the foundation for discussions and written exercises on various economic subjects.
Unit 1 – Start-ups; Unit 2 – The ‘Gig Economy’; Unit 3 – Business Cycle; Unit 4 – Economic Theory in Practice; Unit 5 – Fintech.
90 Euro for WE2A, WE2B, WE2C, and WE2D Keystone (13 double hours, including final exam).

The HIGHER level consists of the parallel courses WE3A – WE3D. All Higher courses have the same level of difficulty (target level B2.2 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages) and are content-wise the same. They are suitable for students who want to deepen their Business English knowledge.
Completion of level B2.1 of the GER or 61 – 80 points in the placement test.
The reading and writing component of the course will be assessed in a 90-minute written exam in the last week of the semester. A graded certificate is issued for passing the exam.

In the Business English Higher course, participants learn vocabulary and expressions specifically for the business world. A variety of exercises aim to promote linguistic and conceptual understanding of current topics and lay the foundation for discussions and written exercises on various economic subjects.
Unit 1 – Future of Work; Unit 2 – Economic Migration; Unit 3 – Poverty; Unit 4 – Philanthropy; Unit 5 – Tax Evasion and Tax Avoidance.
90 Euro for WE3A, WE3B, WE3C, and WE3D Higher (13 double hours, including final exam).
